t: Aleppo first appears in tablets of the third millennium BCE, was the capital of the Amorite kingdom of Yamhad, and was later held by Hittites, Assyrians, Persians, Seleucids, Romans, Arabs, Mongols, Mamluks and Ottomans.

Its position on the trade routes between the Mediterranean and Mesopotamia made it, by the middle of the 16th century, the principal market in the region for goods from the east, with European consulates and the headquarters of the Levant Company.
The Suez Canal, the borders drawn after the First World War and the rise of Damascus drew trade and power away from it, and the war that reached the city in 2012 damaged much of its old city.
dyk: In 1400 Tamerlane captured Aleppo, massacred many of its inhabitants and ordered a tower of 20,000 skulls built outside the city.
ev: Aleppo appears for the first time in the Ebla tablets
The kingdom of Yamhad, with Aleppo as its capital, begins to rise to power
Alexander the Great takes over the city
The Rashidun Muslims under Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah take Aleppo
The Mongols under Hulagu take the city after a siege
Aleppo becomes part of the Ottoman Empire under Selim I
The French declare the State of Aleppo
Rebel forces evacuate eastern Aleppo and the Syrian Army declares full control of the city

f.founded: The city may have been inhabited since the sixth millennium BCE; Amorites occupied the area by the latter part of the third millennium BCE, when Aleppo first appears in cuneiform tablets found at Ebla and in Mesopotamia.
f.where: On a plateau 380 m above sea level, on the Queiq River, about 120 km inland from the Mediterranean Sea, in northern Syria.
f.known: The Amorite kingdom of Yamhad; the temple of the storm god Hadad on the citadel hill; the Hellenistic city of Beroea; the Hamdanid court of Sayf al-Dawla; the Mongol conquest of 1260; the Ottoman trade in silk; the covered souqs and khans of the old city; the battle of 2012 to 2016
f.today: Aleppo is the capital of the Aleppo Governorate and one of the largest cities of Syria.
